item.title: Jamichael Stillwell powers Texas Tech basketball to historic win over Illinois in debut
item.description: Brad Underwood didn't need any film on Jamichael Stillwell with the Texas Tech basketball team to know what he brought to the table. Days after receiving a temporary restraining order from a Lubbock judge, Stillwell made his Red Raider debut, stepping onto the United Supermarkets Arena floor before the first media timeout. A newcomer who Tech fans had never seen play in person (his lone game against Tech while at UCF came in Orlando), Stillwell was greeted to raucous cheers from every corner of the sold-out building. "The fans love me," Stillwell said, "and I love y'all back." Underwood knew the impact Stillwell could have, saying after the game the Atlanta native's penchant for grabbing offensive rebounds was notable in Illinois' scout work on the 6-foot-8 big man. After the 16th-ranked Red Raiders claimed an 84-78 win over third-ranked Illinois — the highest-ranked nonconference opponent at home in Tech history — Underwood looked at the stat sheet and saw Stillwell's final damage: 11 points and 13 rebounds, six of them on the offensive glass. "He literally, physically whipped our butt," Underwood said. "Give him credit. It's a pretty good first game." Grant McCasland has been excited at the prospect of having Stillwell on the floor with this year's team. His first game as a Red Raider showed the reasons why. Rebounding against a much taller and physical Fighting Illini frontcourt. Operating the pick-and-roll with Cruz Davis (game-high 20 points and five assists). Being in the right position more often than not defensively, even switching off onto guards along the perimeter as Texas Tech looked to put the game away. "Jamichael Stillwell's a winner," McCasland said. "I mean, his physicality index is 100. He's amazing at putting his body in the middle of it consistently, and his belief in our team and his command. ... His presence alone in a game like that, you could, it just felt like he settled us, just going up and making free throws." Stillwell has been practicing with the Red Raiders since joining the team in the late summer, initially on a temporary injunction in the state of Georgia. The NCAA earned a stay in that case, so Stillwell dropped out and refiled in Lubbock County last week, being granted a TRO from Judge John Grace, the same judge who awarded Donovan Atwell (13 points, five steals) his temporary injunction in October. Being around the team this whole time, Stillwell said, made jumping in for his first game action easier. "It really started off the court," Stillwell said. "Just with the chemistry, we always got that chemistry, and in practice, we just keep the same chemistry. I'm kind of easy to play with, so it wasn't hard." Davis agreed with Stillwell's assessment of himself. He's easier to play with than most, and offers Texas Tech the ability to clamp down on defense like the team did in the closing minutes to put the game away. Section 4 Class B: Maine-Endwell (7-2) vs. Johnson City (8-2) Game Pick: Johnson City (by a hair) The signs all point to Maine-Endwell: an undefeated division record, including a 28-23 win over JC, an offense averaging 15 yards per reception, and a four-year sectional title streak (2021-2024). item.title: Purdue football's Tra'Mar Harris turns tragedy into breakout success story
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Most run from adversity. Tra'Mar Harris has been living in it for three years. He almost ran from it, too. After two years with Purdue football, where his only time seeing the field was 13 plays on Nov. 8, 2025 against Ohio State in a game that was for all intents and purposes already decided, Harris considered entering the transfer portal. After some self reflection, and a full court press by a persuasive Boilermaker coaching staff, Harris realized Purdue was where he was most comfortable. Somewhere, Deasia Wynn is smiling and shouting her trademark phrase, "that's what's up." Wynn is a primary reason Harris chose Purdue in the first place. She celebrated her 26th birthday accompanying her little brother on a recruiting visit to West Lafayette. By the end of the night, Wynn told Harris Purdue was the right place for him. The star receiver at Winton Woods High School in Cincinnati committed to the Boilermakers a week later, choosing them over more than 20 other Division I scholarship offers . By the time Harris enrolled at Purdue in January 2024 at age 17, his sister had been gone for more than two months, the victim of a cold-blooded murder while in her sleep. "They were very close. She came to all his games, supported him, took him to practice. He went to her house every other weekend to stay the night," said Tra'Mar's mother, Trina Scott-Harris. "She was like the little momma bear." Tra'Mar Harris hurting, healing through football The Harris household's world revolved around sports. Parents Markus and Trina were athletes. The oldest child, Chuck Wynn, played college football at Eastern Kentucky and Urbana University, and coincidentally enough made his first career tackle against Purdue in Ross-Ade Stadium. Deasia was a basketball standout, a pure shooter with a quick step and unmatched strength that offset her limitations in speed and leaping ability. She played collegiately for Miami University-Hamilton and Ohio State-Mansfield. Her No. 15 is retired at Winton Woods High School. The youngest, Jayden Harris, is a junior at Winton Woods, where he's a multi-sport athlete. The one athletic feat that will never be matched, though, came from Tra'Mar Harris on Oct. 20, 2023. It was the day after Deasia Wynn was senselessly shot . At 3 o'clock that afternoon news spread that Wynn was killed at the hands of her childhood best friend. Coaches told Harris he didn't have to play, but the then-senior at Winton Woods needed an escape and football was about to provide it for Harris and his family. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. item.title: NFL trade deadline winners and losers: Vikings go full dadcore with Kirk Cousins in Super Bowl quest
item.description: Kirk Cousins is heading back to the Minnesota Vikings. Photograph: Justine Willard/AP The Vikings get the QB they desperately need After what happened on Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings had to do this. In a dispiriting loss to the Buffalo Bills, the Vikings saw their tremendous defense go to waste, as Carson Wentz completed eight of 25 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 8.9. It was one of the worst quarterback performances in recent history , and it continued a run of recent QB futility for the Vikings, from JJ McCarthy to Kyler Murray to Wentz. Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is out-scheming every other coach in the league right now with his laboratory of blitzes and coverages. But it’s starting to matter less and less, because opposing offenses know that you can wait that defense out when there’s no juice on the other side of the ball. The Vikings rank first in scoring defense (116 points allowed), but they’re 27th in points scored (146). This is not sustainable, which is why Minnesota welcomed ur-suburban dad Kirk Cousins back to the team he led from 2018-2023 by sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders . The 38-year-old is in his 15th NFL season, and he’s not quite the player he used to be, but he’s a massive improvement over everyone else in the Vikings building at his position. This season, Cousins has completed 202 of 315 passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns, eight interceptions, and a passer rating of 97.1. The rest of the Vikings QBs this season have combined for 137 of 225 passes for 1,286 yards, eight touchdowns, five interceptions, and a passer rating of 82.0. Cousins enters an NFC North that may be the most brutally competitive division in NFL history , but if he plays like he has this season so far, the Vikings have more than a puncher’s chance. Do the Vikings like that ? We suspect that they do. And in addition to his play on the field, he should bring a maturity and calm to the quarterback position in Minnesota, something that McCarthy and Murray’s critics have said they have lacked at points during their careers. item.title: Man Utd open talks with Pochettino about replacing Carrick
item.description: Michael Carrick is set to depart as Manchester United manager, with Mauricio Pochettino in talks to replace him [Getty Images] Manchester United have opened talks with USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino about replacing Michael Carrick, who is expected to lose his job this week. Carrick's future at United will be decided at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday that will be attended by chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe. And discussions for former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino to return to the Premier League are under way. United have spoken to the ex-Argentina defender about their managerial position on three previous occasions - when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 before the club appointed Erik ten Hag and again when the Dutchman was sacked in 2024. Pochettino renewed his contract with the USA in August, and they have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week. The 54-year-old has a $10m (£7.5m) release clause. Berrada and Wilcox have flown to Monaco for one of their regular, planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club. On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next. It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go. United are 18th in the Premier League - inside the relegation zone - after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August. It is the club's lowest position at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when they were 20th. item.description: Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha warms up ahead of the Premier League match at Selhurst Park, London. Picture date: Sunday November 8, 2026. (Photo by John Walton/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Liverpool FC attacker Rio Ngumoha is the subject of a profile in The Telegraph , and there are some pretty interesting quotes in the piece. The article leads with Harry Kane’s Ballon D’or win, and if he thinks he can win it one day. He answered yes, duh. The rest of it explores Ngumoha’s journey from Manor Park, Newham, a borough of London to Chelsea’s academy. It’s worth a read. The latter half of the piece gets into Ngumoha’s reasons for leaving Chelsea and joining the Reds: “I feel like I needed a new challenge. I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea… I’m not saying that I wouldn’t have got to the first team as quick, because I believe in my ability, but I feel like Liverpool just gave me a new pathway. “The plan that they set for me was straightforward really. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool, and they just said if I prove myself, because they know how much ability I had, then they know that I would definitely be a first-team player and definitely a star for them in the making. I think going to Liverpool so far has been the right choice.” Again, he speaks of the sacrifice his mother has had to go through to facilitate his move to Liverpool: “My mum has done a lot for me. The hardest thing for her has been moving up to Liverpool. She left her job in a school to move up three or four months after me. But I think she’s enjoying it as well. It’s definitely been tough as she has friends in London. She goes back whenever she can. But she does everything for me and my brother. She’s just amazing. I can’t thank her enough.” Rio also spoke about his experience with the England national team setup so far, and with Thomas Tuchel specifically: “When I first came [with England], I was a bit shy, so I was keeping myself to myself,” said Ngumoha. “But then they got me in the group. The shyness goes from the first time you touch the ball and step on the pitch. Then you realise it’s just football and you can play the way you play. After the first session, it goes.” “I think it’s very nice. He knows I’m quite talented, which is good. Every time I come on, he lets me be expressive, be free. He also coaches me as well. Off the ball, on the ball, little ideas. I just have the belief from him and all the coaches here. It’s top. Hopefully I can just keep going and keep leaving a good impression on him.” It’s been a big year for Rio. Let’s hope even bigger and better things are in store for Rio as he continues to be fearless.

It must be remembered that Barcelona were among several European clubs monitoring Nijstad during the summer transfer window. item.title: Next Man United manager: Who could replace Michael Carrick?
item.description: Michael Carrick appears to be on the brink of being sacked by Manchester United , with the club inside the relegation zone during the international break and considering a fourth permanent manager in three years since minority owners Ineos, under Sir Jim Ratcliffe, took control of football operations. Carrick – who impressed during his interim spell in charge last season – has seen the goodwill this season evaporate after United’s worst start to a season in 40 years , with a disastrous defensive performance seeing them go two goals down against Aston Villa before a miraculous late comeback earned a 4-4 draw. Liverpool away after the international break offers little hope of escaping the drop zone, before a trip to Lisbon in the Champions League. While the problems United face run far deeper than the head coach – as highlighted by defender Lisandro Martinez after the defeat to Atletico Madrid earlier this month – while criticism of Carrick’s tactics came from United captain Bruno Fernandes , who has not been able to inspire the team in the manner that saw him pick up the PFA Player of the Year award and the league’s assist record last term. So if United do finally pull the trigger on another change of manager, who could be in charge at Anfield and beyond in a bid to, firstly, guide the club away from a relegation battle? Mauricio Pochettino The current odds-on favourite after emerging as a key target , yet Man United could face a problem getting the Argentine out of his United States contract, having committed to terms up to the next World Cup in 2030. Compensation in excess of £7m could follow, yet United are in a desperate situation and the experience and presence of Pochettino could spark a reaction from a group desperately short of inspiration. Pochettino’s powers have waned since his famous spell with Spurs, though his exit at Chelsea came at the end of a promising run to conclude the 2023/24 season. There was immense potential and excitement to start the 2026 World Cup, but a combination of the Folarin Balogun scandal and then a thumping at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 took the shine off Pochettino’s performance from the dugout. Now, it remains to be seen if he can deliver once more in club football in what would surely be his most difficult job to date. Eddie Howe The Englishman is available after his shock decision to leave Newcastle United in the summer . Howe told the club he needed a break from management but the chance to take charge at Old Trafford, three months later, would surely be too good to turn down if an offer arrives. item.title: Kane not ruling out Premier League return despite Bayern extension
item.description: Kane not ruling out Premier League return despite Bayern extension Bayern Munich recently announced a contract extension for Harry Kane until 2029, at which point the England captain will be 36 years old. With the new deal, Kane committed his immediate future to FC Bayern, but his new contract doesn't necessarily mean he intends to see out the remainder of his career in Munich, despite being very happy at the club. There has been ongoing speculation that Kane could one day return to the Premier League in a bid to surpass Alan Shearer's all-time record of 260 goals, with the former Tottenham striker having already netted 213 times in the English top-flight. Speaking to Sport Bild, Kane refused to rule out the possibility of returning to the Premier League in the future, although he made it clear that it is not something he is currently focused on. “My focus is currently on Bayern. We have a great team and a fantastic coach, and I am extremely happy here. Of course, we still have further ambitions with Bayern and want to achieve new things. Above all, we want to win the Champions League, continue to dominate the Bundesliga and defend the titles we won last season,” Kane said, adding: “Throughout my career and my life, I have learned that you cannot always control everything yourself. Sometimes you simply have to let things take their course, believe in yourself and continue to work hard. That is my top priority at the moment. I would never rule out breaking the Premier League's all-time goalscoring record at some point. item.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to the Netherlands
item.description: Tatjana Smith won a gold and silver medal at each of the past two Olympics [Getty Images] South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched her international allegiance to the Netherlands. The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games. She chose to come out of retirement in September, hoping to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles. But Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow". Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch and said "I've always been Dutch and South African", adding that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport". She also said it also offers her "the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport. Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment. Having initially chosen to represent the country of her birth, Smith claimed four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023. She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024. "Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media. "The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow. "This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of. "I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me." Smith said she will continue to live and train in South Africa and is set to represent the Dutch team for the first time at the short course world championships from 1-6 December. item.title: Germany's Ter Stegen: Starting position at Euro 2028 not a guarantee
item.description: FILE PHOTO - German goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen in action during the team's training session ahead of the UEFA Nations League soccer match against the Netherlands. (is associated with: «Germany's Ter Stegen: Starting position at Euro 2028 not a guarantee») Federico Gambarini/dpa Goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen doesn't want to assume that he's guaranteed a spot in Germany's starting line-up for Euro 2028. "That's what the past has taught me. I don't want to think about what will happen in two years," he told Wednesday's Sport Bild weekly. Ter Stegen returned to the national team during the international break in October and November. It was his first time with the team since June 2025. He was supposed to be Manuel Neuer's replacement, after the latter retired following Euro 2024. But a back injury, followed by a thigh injury, not only saw him losing his spot in the national team and this year's World Cup, but also his starting position at Barcelona. Ter Stegen still has a contract with the Spanish club until 2028, but after a six-month loan to Girona, he's now on loan at Ajax. Germany face Serbia in the Nations League on Friday and Ter Stegen is expected to be the starting goalkeeper. But until Euro 2028, he will have to compete at least with Besiktas' Alexander Nübel and Bayern Munich talent Jonas Urbig. "I'm excited to get to know Jonas better and see him in action during training," Ter Stegen said. The veteran goalkeeper, however, sees his experience as a boost to his aim of becoming Germany's number one. "We recently haven't had the best phase with the national team. Many people are quick to demand that we bring in new players, that all the youngsters have to be included. I think that's generally good and right, but there will also be difficult moments, and then experience will be important," he said.

item.title: Raphinha had surgery after El Clasico to avoid missing Brazil friendlies

item.title: Vitor Reis: "Happy and delighted to be part of Brazil's new era”
item.description: Vitor Reis: "Happy and delighted to be part of Brazil's new era” Center-back Vitor Reis expressed his delight at being part of what he called a “new era” for the Brazilian national team. At 20, the defender is among the players involved in Brazil’s rebuilding process since the last World Cup, and he praised the supportive atmosphere that allows him and the other youngsters to show their potential. "I'm happy and delighted to be part of this new era for the national team. I'm also very happy to reunite with teammates I've played with at clubs and in the youth national teams. I believe we young players have a lot of potential, and everyone in the national team gives us the peace of mind to do our jobs and show why we're here. It's a dream come true for all of us," he said enthusiastically at a press conference on Wednesday (11). He highlighted the importance of playing alongside center-backs established in European football and the Brazilian national team, such as Gabriel Magalhães, who is in the current squad, and Marquinhos, his idol, whom he joined during the recent international windows in September and October. He said the lessons he learns help him grow both as a footballer and as a person. "In training, we try to learn as much as possible from the defenders. Gabriel does a phenomenal job at his club and here. The last time I was here, I played with Marquinhos, who has been my idol since I was little. Playing with people like that helps you grow not just as a footballer, but as a person too," he said. Vitor Reis during a press conference with the Brazilian national team in Singapore Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF "It's very important for us to have these pillars of the team. There are a lot of young players, and we need these role models to grow and develop. Marquinhos and Gabriel Magalhães put us at ease and help us on the pitch. They're also phenomenal people," he added. Although still young in the senior national team, Vitor has extensive experience with Brazil's youth teams. Between 2022 and 2024, he was part of Brazil's Under-16, Under-17 and Under-20 squads. During that time, he won the South American Under-17 Championship in 2023 alongside forward Rayan, who has been called up by Ancelotti, and Phillipe Gabriel, who was brought in to help with goalkeeper preparations. He explained that he brings this experience to the senior national team. "It helps us a lot. We begin to understand the significance of this shirt and the Brazilian national team, and that helps us grow. It's very important to follow that path through the national teams. I won the South American Under-17 Championship and was captain. I also played in the Under-17 World Cup, and wearing the captain's armband was very rewarding for me. item.title: Jacobo Ramon explains why he decided to leave Real Madrid after 12 years at the club: ‘I knew my time had come’
item.description: Jacobo Ramon explains why he decided to leave Real Madrid after 12 years at the club: ‘I knew my time had come’ Real Madrid have seen several promising academy graduates establish themselves away from the Santiago Bernabeu in recent seasons. The biggest name among them is Nico Paz, who has gone on to become a superstar in Serie A for Como. Another player whose career has followed a steady upward trajectory is Jacobo Ramon, who plays for the same club as Paz. The 21-year-old has been going from strength to strength over the last couple of seasons and has now earned his maiden call-up to the senior Spain squad. Jacobo Ramon explains his Real Madrid departure Speaking to MARCA , Ramon has explained why he decided to leave his boyhood club after spending 12 years at La Fabrica . “I knew my time had come,” Ramon admitted, reflecting on the difficult decision to leave Madrid, where he had been developing since the age of eight. “It’s very difficult to break into the first team. The competition is enormous, and I felt I needed to show elsewhere what kind of player I was,” he explained. Jacobo Ramon has performed exceedingly well at Como. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images) The youngster had already experienced first-team football at Madrid but understood that establishing himself as a regular starter would be considerably more challenging. Rather than continuing to wait for occasional opportunities, Ramon decided that moving elsewhere would provide the experience necessary to accelerate his development. “I took the right step at the right time, and so far, it’s working out well for me,” he added. Cesc Fabregas played a crucial role in his decision Ramon revealed that Fabregas personally contacted him to explain Como’s ambitious project and how he would fit into the team’s playing style. “Cesc called me, explained his idea of football, and I felt it suited the type of player I am perfectly,” the defender explained. The opportunity to develop under a manager who prioritises possession and building attacks from the back was particularly appealing to Ramon. Cesc has been instrumental in developing Jacobo Ramon. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) It is safe to say he made the perfect decision to join Cesc’s ambitious project, which continues to grow. Real Madrid have a buy-back clause for Ramon next summer and could look to bring him back for the upcoming season. Los Blancos could look to re-sign him and sell him back to Como for a higher fee, as they did with Paz last summer. Alternatively, Jose Mourinho could decide to include Ramon in his first-team plans and give him opportunities to impress next season.

It also means another cross-country move for his family, and his wife, Julie Cousins, is already documenting the emotional transition. Hours after Tuesday’s blockbuster trade with the Las Vegas Raiders, Julie shared a series of Instagram Stories showing the family’s final moments in Las Vegas before departing for Minnesota. One of those posts featured Cousins wearing his old Vikings uniform, accompanied by the message, “Another adventure awaits…” The veteran quarterback subsequently reshared the Story on his own Instagram account, adding a personal touch to a reunion that has dominated NFL headlines since the November 10 trade deadline. But it was another post featuring the couple’s son, Turner, that revealed just how quickly life is changing for the Cousins family. (Instagram/@juliehcousins) Kirk Cousins’ Wife Julie Shares Emotional Goodbye to Las Vegas In a separate Instagram Story, Julie posted footage of Turner participating in a nighttime Little League baseball game in Las Vegas. With the family preparing to leave Nevada, Turner apparently had one final request before moving back to Minnesota. “1 hour until we leave for Minnesota… Turner wanted one last at bat in his little league playoff game,” Julie wrote, adding a heart-eyes emoji. She concluded the message with a heartfelt farewell: “We love you, Las Vegas!” The post offered an intimate glimpse into the reality of an NFL trade, particularly one involving a player with a wife and young children. item.title: Remember the 2025 Gautam Gambhir-Oval groundsman spat? Lee Fortis leaves Surrey after disciplinary proceedings over ECB employee altercation
item.description: NEW DELHI: Lee Fortis, who worked as Surrey's head groundsman for more than a decade, has left the club after facing disciplinary proceedings over his conduct. The club had sent Fortis on indefinite leave in late July after he had an argument with an England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) employee. The incident happened a day before MI London took on London Spirit in The Hundred at the Oval. Fortis also had a strong exchange with Surrey chief executive Steve Elworthy, a former South Africa fast bowler, soon after the incident. He did not return to work for the rest of the summer. Fortis joined Surrey in 2012. His LinkedIn profile now shows that he left the club in October and is "open to work". A Surrey spokesperson told Telegraph Sport: "Lee Fortis has left the club and we wish him well for the future." Fortis' earlier clash with Gautam Gambhir Fortis had also been in the news in 2025 after an argument with India head coach Gautam Gambhir. The two had a disagreement over the Oval pitch. During the exchange, Gambhir told Fortis: "You’re just a groundsman, nothing beyond that." India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak later called Fortis "arrogant". Fortis, who is around 6ft 10in tall, was a well-known face in English cricket. He became Surrey's head groundsman in 2012 at the age of 30. His work also brought him recognition. He won the top award at the ECB's Grounds Manager of the Year Awards three years in a row, from 2022 to 2024. Surrey won the County Championship in all three seasons. What led to Fortis being placed on leave? Fortis was known for speaking directly and firmly to his staff and other people at the Oval. The incident in July was not the first time he had been involved in a disagreement. The Cricket Regulator was reported to have started an investigation into the matter. However, it did not comment when Telegraph Sport contacted it on Tuesday. The details and findings of the disciplinary proceedings have not been made public. Surrey face search for new groundsman Surrey will now have to find someone to take Fortis's place. The search comes at an important time for the club, with the Oval set to host two major Test matches next season. The ground will stage the World Test Championship final in June, followed by the fifth Ashes Test in late July. Surrey are expected to begin looking for a replacement in the coming weeks. Gary Barwell of Warwickshire is among the names being considered for the job. The club also had a tough 2026 season. After finishing in the top two of the County Championship for four seasons in a row, Surrey found themselves fighting to stay in the division towards the end of the campaign. There was also a change in the coaching staff. Gareth Batty left his role as head coach after five years and joined Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League. Surrey are looking for a new head coach, but Rory Burns is expected to remain captain for the 2027 season. It will be his 10th year as club captain.

item.description: PHILADELPHIA — The 2026-27 NBA season is still in its infancy, so the games don't carry quite as much weight as they will in April, May, and June. But, Tuesday night's meeting between the Boston Celtics and rival Philadelphia 76ers was jam-packed with emotions, giving it a playoff atmosphere in the middle of November. Most of this buildup began in the offseason, as the C's shockingly traded star guard Jaylen Brown to the Sixers in exchange for veteran wing Paul George and a few picks. Brown, who was the longest-tenured Celtic at the time of the deal, was obviously upset by the stunning move. And based on some of his activity on social media, he also seems upset that Tatum, his old partner in crime, didn't prevent the trade from happening. Then the new season finally started, and Brown took a few shots at his ex-teammate on Instagram and in front of the media. However, Tatum looked willing to forget the aforementioned saga when he approached Brown just seconds before tipoff on Tuesday evening. A bit of an awkward dap up for Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. But LeBron James brings it in with Tatum: pic.twitter.com/vgkgqRWaVs — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) November 11, 2026 The Celtics star performed his usual routine by the sidelines, dapped up Sixers star Joel Embiid, and then advanced towards Brown for a hug. Yet, the former Green Teamer didn't budge, spinning the ball on his finger while Tatum had to walk away following the failed greeting. "No headlines about anything like that," Tatum said of the awkward encounter at the podium. "I was just getting ready for the game, ready for jump ball, go out there and compete, have some fun, and try to get a win.” In some ways, this moment encapsulated each star's approach to the marquee matchup. Tatum appeared ready to let bygones be bygones and move past controversy. Brown, whether he meant to or not, fanned the flames of the supposed beef when he ignored Tatum, perhaps revealing that he was still somewhat occupied with the aforementioned drama rather than the imminent game. Brown played like he was distracted, too. The five-time All-Star got into early foul trouble, recorded a team-high 4 turnovers, and held the worst plus-minus rating of the night (minus-27). Meanwhile, Tatum settled into the game and dropped 21 points — 8 more than Brown — en route to a 123-101 victory for the Celtics. Neither star was at their best, but Tatum played more composed, led the C's in assists, and found George at all the right times. That includes when Brown went to double-team Tatum about halfway through the fourth quarter, leaving George completely alone for an easy 3-pointer. This mistake made the score 111-87, virtually sealing the win, and was George's final triple of the evening. He finished with a game-high 36 points on blistering 63.6 shooting from the floor. item.title: Nick Wright tears into Vikings’ Kirk Cousins trade with brutal Kevin O’Connell verdict
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images Nick Wright has delivered a brutal assessment of the Minnesota Vikings’ decision to trade for Kirk Cousins, accusing head coach Kevin O’Connell of creating the quarterback problem he is now trying to fix. Minnesota sent the Las Vegas Raiders a 2027 third-round pick to bring Cousins back after struggling to find consistency at the position. The move has divided opinion, with some viewing the veteran as the stability the Vikings desperately need. However, Wright believes the trade exposes a series of costly decisions made by the organisation, particularly under O’Connell’s leadership. Nick Wright calls Minnesota Vikings’ quarterback decisions ‘catastrophic team building’ Speaking on First Things First, Wright acknowledged that Cousins could help Minnesota become a legitimate contender if he maintains his recent form. But he was far less complimentary about the process that brought the Vikings back to their former quarterback. “This is one of the most mortifying sequence of transactions for a team I’ve ever seen,” Wright said. He then questioned the decision to move on from Cousins in the first place, before criticising the handling of Kyler Murray and the draft capital Minnesota had to spend to bring the veteran back. “This is catastrophic team building. Kevin O’Connell does not get credit for now having the potential to put out a fire that he started, added gasoline to, and then told the fire department to turn around.” The criticism comes after Minnesota moved on from Cousins following the 2023 campaign and drafted J.J. McCarthy as his potential successor. McCarthy missed his first season through injury, while Sam Darnold subsequently led the Vikings to a 14-3 record before leaving for Seattle, where he won a Super Bowl. Minnesota later moved on from McCarthy as well, with the quarterback finding opportunities with the New York Giants. Kyler Murray then struggled before his injury, while Carson Wentz failed to provide the required consistency. Cousins arrives with 2,340 passing yards and 20 touchdowns, ranking fifth and second respectively in those categories. The Vikings have struggled offensively, ranking 31st in total offence with 266.8 yards per game and 31st in passing offence with 160.8. Former NFL linebacker Emmanuel Acho has also questioned whether Cousins can take Minnesota all the way, arguing he is capable of getting the team to the playoffs rather than guaranteeing a Super Bowl. With the Green Bay Packers next on the schedule, Cousins will have an immediate opportunity to show whether he can give O’Connell’s offence the lift it needs. item.title: Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as Carrick replacement
item.description: Manchester United finalising deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as Carrick replacement Manchester United are finalising a deal to hire Mauricio Pochettino, the reliable David Ornstein of The Athletic has revealed. Pochettino interest It’s looking increasingly likely that Michael Carrick will be sacked, owing to United’s awful form so far this season. Sunday’s dramatic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left the club in 18th place, a largely novel and unfathomable position for United; however, the performances and results indicate that this reality is not shocking. The Red Devils have won just one game, drawn five and lost four. They boast a meagre eight points from their opening 10 games. A meeting is set to take place in Monaco today between Sir Jim Ratcliffe and club executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox. The expectation is that Berrada and Wilcox will recommend that Carrick be dismissed . The legendary midfielder no longer enjoys the support of the top brass and will be let go. Pochettino has emerged as a leading candidate for the Old Trafford hot seat and it’s believed that he is very keen on the opportunity. He has long coveted the role and come close on several occasions, yet nothing has ever materialised. Now, Ornstein reports that Pochettino is just one step away from becoming the next United boss. Pochettino bombshell Ornstein writes for The Athletic , “Manchester United are finalising a deal for Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, if an ultimate decision is taken to relieve Michael Carrick of his duties.” “Amid a sequence of only three wins in 15 games, work has been undertaken on potential successors and Pochettino — the United States men’s national team boss — has emerged as the chosen candidate.” “Sources with knowledge of the process, speaking on the condition of anonymity to protect relationships, have told The Athletic that United spent Tuesday ironing out personal terms with the Argentine’s representatives — no issues are anticipated — but they have yet to contact U.S. Soccer, to whom an exit clause worth around $10million (£7.4m) would need to be paid.” Ornstein adds that if United decide to press ahead with Pochettino’s appointment, he will be joined by his USMNT coaching staff. United would fork out a larger compensation to also get them out of their contracts. Pochettino’s current terms with the USMNT run until 2030. He has previously managed in the Premier League, taking charge of Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea. His most recent club stint was with Paris Saint-Germain.

item.title: Stats behind Fermin Lopez’s special quality that makes him difficult to defend
item.description: Stats behind Fermin Lopez’s special quality that makes him difficult to defend Barcelona midfielder Fermin Lopez is enjoying one of the most productive periods of his career under Hansi Flick, with eight goals and seven assists in 15 appearances across competitions in the 2026/27 season. Understandably, the 23-year-old has become an increasingly important member of Flick’s squad, taking advantage of Dani Olmo’s injury to establish greater consistency in the starting line-up. His attacking output is particularly impressive because of his ability to finish with either foot and with his header. Since his debut under former manager Xavi , Fermin’s development as a two-footed goalscorer has become an important weapon for Barcelona, making him difficult for opposition defenders to predict and contain. Dani Olmo’s injury has opened the door for Fermin Fermin’s increased involvement following Olmo’s injury has coincided with an outstanding run of individual performances. Fermin Lopez can score from anywhere and with both feet. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) His ability to contribute goals and assists from midfield has given Flick another attacking option, particularly when Barcelona need late runs into the penalty area. As such, the numbers help explain his development, as he scored 11 goals in 2023/24, followed by eight goals and nine assists in 2024/25. He subsequently registered 13 goals and 17 assists during the 2025/26 campaign, putting his current eight goals and seven assists in a strong position to challenge those previous seasonal totals. Furthermore, one of Fermin’s biggest strengths is his ability to finish with either foot. Statistically, 23 of his 45 goals have come with his right foot, 17 from his left and five from headers. Flick has a strong attacking weapon Fermin Lopez has become crucial to Barcelona’s attacking setup. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Fermin’s contribution to the team is not limited to goals. Indeed, they are important, but his versatility also gives Barcelona an advantage beyond his goalscoring numbers. On that note, it is crucial to remember that he can operate in attacking midfield, in deep central areas and can also play out wide if required, although he has not played there this season thanks to the depth Flick has at his disposal. What has stood out this season is his ability to arrive late inside the penalty area and threaten goal from different shooting angles. On top of that, his ability to use both feet makes those movements even more difficult to defend. Simply put, while the likes of Lamine Yamal and Raphinha are hogging the limelight, and for all the right reasons, Barcelona have another offensive threat who can influence matches, just as he did against Atletico Madrid .

item.description: Real Madrid-linked midfielder breaks silence on transfer rumours amid current struggles: ‘Haven’t contacted anyone’ Real Madrid have undergone a significant transformation under Jose Mourinho, with Los Blancos securing eight straight victories ahead of the international break. The Portuguese manager has made some tactical tweaks to bring greater balance to midfield and defence. However, midfield remains an area of concern for Los Blancos , who could look to strengthen it in the future. One player who has been heavily linked with a move to the Santiago Bernabeu is Martin Zubimendi. His difficult situation at Arsenal and lack of playing time have prompted discussion about whether Real Madrid could make a move for him in the summer. Zubimendi addresses Real Madrid speculation However, speaking to MARCA , the Spanish international played down suggestions that he could leave London any time soon. The midfielder was asked whether Madrid’s recent resurgence had reduced their need to sign a player of his profile in the immediate future. Zubimendi acknowledged how quickly perceptions change in football and explained that this was normal at a club like Madrid. Real Madrid’s midfield situation has changed Zubimendi had previously attracted considerable interest from Los Blancos , even before his move to London. However, Mourinho’s arrival has brought greater clarity to Madrid’s midfield structure, with Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler increasingly influential. item.description: Northern Ireland are top of Nations League Group B2 after four games [Getty Images] Despite being together for 16 straight days only a month ago, when Northern Ireland players reconvened this week for Nations League fixtures against Ukraine and Hungary there was still plenty of catching up to do. Whether it be Pierce Charles' incredible double-save of Jarrod Bowen's penalty to preserve a point for Queens Park Rangers against West Ham, Isaac Price putting his own spot-kick woe behind him back at West Bromwich Albion, or Terry Devlin's double for Portsmouth against Swansea, there have been memorable moments aplenty for Michael O'Neill's squad back in club colours. Most pleasing to the manager, however, will likely be the game time currently enjoyed by his players. O'Neill has never shied away from the importance of a player's club situation to their international ambitions and, almost four years after his return to the Northern Ireland job, the message has clearly hit home. Of what is a 24-man squad for games against Ukraine on Saturday and Hungary three days later, nine players made either a permanent or loan switch during the summer. And while once the former Stoke City boss had to heavily rely on players who were getting precious few minutes in between international windows, now the group is full of regulars across England top three divisions. Excluding the uncapped trio of Dermot Mee, Eoin Kenny and Braiden Graham, the remainder of the panel for this double-header have averaged over 1,000 minutes of club action during the 2026-27 campaign. Of that group, only Tom Atcheson, who has been carrying a knock, Paddy McNair, Kieran Morrison and Callum Marshall have started fewer than four games since the side's most recent international against Georgia last month. The next step, O'Neill feels, is to have more and more joining the likes of Conor Bradley, Daniel Ballard, Trai Hume and Shea Charles in the Premier League. "There's a lot of players who are playing on a regular basis at their clubs, which is a real positive," said O'Neill, who is without Ballard, Bradley and Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill for this window through injuries. "I think at this stage of their career they should be looking up. Our players that play in the Championship hopefully will have aspirations to play in the Premier League, and I think we have players that are capable of that. "A lot of these players are still around that 20, 21, 22 age group but they're capable of taking that step. "The more players we can get to the Premier League will help us as a nation, there's no doubt about that.
